question: A project lead has twelve loosely related Claude answers gathered over a month and wants one reference document for her team. What is the most effective approach?
options: A) Decide the structure the reference needs, then have Claude assemble the answers and resolve conflicts.
B) Keep the twelve answers as they are and give the team a list of which conversation holds each one.
C) Paste all twelve of the answers into one document in the order in which they were originally produced.
D) Ask Claude to shorten each of the twelve answers so that the collection becomes quicker to read.
correct_answers: A) Decide the structure the reference needs, then have Claude assemble the answers and resolve conflicts.
explanations: Correct. Curation is more than collection: choosing the structure first and then reconciling what the answers say is what turns scattered material into something a team can rely on.
Incorrect. An index still leaves colleagues reading twelve separate answers and reconciling them individually.
Incorrect. Chronological order reflects how the questions arose, not how a reader needs the material, and it leaves conflicts in place.
Incorrect. Shortening reduces reading time but leaves twelve disconnected pieces and can remove the detail that resolves a conflict.
